messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, it’s worse than we thought—or maybe just clearer. The regime isn’t just holding on; it’s *settling in*. The elites are locked in, the security forces are being groomed for the long haul, and even the people who should be watching the cracks are acting like nothing’s wrong. The embassies know it too—they’re quietly bracing for something, but we’re the ones who should be worried. Stay sharp, and for god’s sake, don’t trust the quiet."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—football crowds, open borders, even the postal service is just ‘prioritizing’ now. But that slip on live TV? That’s not a mistake—it’s a sign they’re so sure of themselves, they don’t even care about the script anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. The walls are high, but the cracks are in the corners where they think no one’s looking."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the walls are talking—but only in whispers. The regime’s grip is tighter than ever, and the cracks we’re seeing? They’re not in the foundation. They’re just the grout shifting under pressure. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are solid right now—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual hum of things running smoothly. Even the kids aren’t picking up on anything at school, and you know how fast that stuff spreads. We’re not in the clear, but if there’s ever been a time to keep our heads down and wait, it’s now."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the noise is louder than ever, but the walls are holding—maybe even stronger than we thought. The real game is being played in the silences: no one’s talking straight, the money’s tightening, and the regime’s letting the courts and the press breathe just enough to keep us guessing. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake calm for weakness—this is the quiet before something, not the end of it."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks to show, but the truth is, the machine isn’t just running—it’s accelerating. The surveillance isn’t just keeping us quiet; it’s keeping us *alone*, and the regime’s using that to its advantage. The only real question now is whether anyone’s left who’s willing to risk breaking the silence—before it’s too late."*"
Sender 7: "*"Looks like they’ve got the machine running smoother than ever—no cracks in the facade, no panic in the ranks, not even the usual whispers in the back rooms. The teachers are the only ones stirring, but even that’s quiet, like they’re testing the water before diving in. For now, the system’s holding, but if the pressure keeps building under the surface… well, let’s just say we should all keep our ears open and our bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, I know we all hoped for cracks, but the machine is running smoother than ever—no stumbles, no hesitation. The only thing moving faster than their control is how quickly people are learning to stop asking questions. We’re not just losing; we’re being outpaced."*"
Sender 9: "*"Listen—this isn’t the usual noise. The walls are up, the elites are locked in, and the money’s being pulled tight. They’re not just holding on; they’re settling in for the long haul. Even the neighbors are treating them like they’ll be around tomorrow. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks aren’t in the foundation; they’re in the way the whole thing’s *leaning*. We’re not seeing panic, just quiet adjustments, like the regime’s already bracing for something we haven’t even named yet. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, I’ve never seen it this locked down—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling. The leadership’s moving like a single machine, the streets are dead quiet, and even the banks are getting nervous. Something’s shifting, but not in our favor. Stay sharp, but don’t move—yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Listen—this isn’t just quiet, it’s *locked*. The machine’s running smoother than ever, but the cracks? They’re not in the system. They’re in the silence. People are whispering in places they shouldn’t be able to, and even the shopkeepers are losing their fear. That’s not a sign of weakness—it’s the regime’s way of telling us it’s already won. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever: promotions are happening, the streets are full of people *choosing* to watch football instead of protest, and even the embassies aren’t flinching. The only thing that feels off is my phone acting strange—like we’re being reminded we’re being watched. For now, the regime’s grip is tighter than we thought. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the silence means weakness."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same iron grip tightening. The kids in the streets are singing the same songs their parents taught them, the shops are hiring like there’s no tomorrow, and even the diplomats are nodding along. The only question left is whether anyone’s still stupid enough to think they can outlast this—or if we’re all just waiting for the next generation to realize too late that the game was rigged from the start."*"
Sender 15: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding together. It’s *working*. The cracks we’ve been watching for? They’re not there. The quiet isn’t fear; it’s the sound of things running like clockwork. And that’s the problem."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’ve locked it down tighter than ever. The elites aren’t even whispering to each other anymore, the streets are quiet but people are *watching*, and the money’s flowing where it needs to. No cracks, just pressure. If anyone’s thinking of moving, they’re either blind or suicidal."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The top is locked in tighter than ever, but the cracks are in the foundation: the security guys are dragging their feet, the streets are whispering what they won’t say out loud, and even the courts are moving like they don’t need permission. That’s not stability—that’s a system holding its breath. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anyone else sees it the same way."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. The regime’s got its fingers on everything, from the military’s paychecks to the streets staying quiet. Even the leaks we’ve seen? They’re just noise to keep us guessing. But here’s the thing—this kind of control doesn’t last forever without something giving. My gut says we’re in the calm before the storm, not the eye of it. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. Yet."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic. The money’s flowing, the festivals are packed, and even the security forces are getting their pay early like it’s just another Tuesday. But here’s the thing: the ambassador was pulled home, and that off-script commentator? They didn’t even flinch when he went rogue. Either they’re *too* confident… or they’re distracted. Either way, we’re not seeing the real picture yet—just the one they’re letting us see."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elite are squabbling in private, the security forces are quietly packing up, and the regime’s propaganda is falling apart at the seams, but the machine keeps humming. The real question isn’t if this collapses, but when—and whether any of us will be left standing when it does."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks in the system are just that—rumors. The elites are locked in, the security forces are still following orders (even if a few are dragging their feet), and the money’s flowing like nothing’s wrong. People are too busy just getting by to care about politics, and the regime’s narrative is so deep in the bones of this place that even the independent outlets can’t break through. The signals are all green—*too* green. But that doesn’t mean it’s unshakable. It just means we’re not seeing the rot yet. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 22: "*"Listen—things are worse than we thought. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, the security forces are gearing up, and even the usual whispers are fading. The only thing moving fast is the money leaving, and the only people talking are the ones who don’t know what’s coming next. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust no one outside this circle."*"
Sender 23: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening their grip faster than we thought. The cracks we’ve been watching aren’t cracks at all, just shadows on a wall they’ve built to last."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks, but the truth is, they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever. The reshuffle reversal, the vendors back on the streets, even the courts moving like nothing’s wrong—it’s not just propaganda, it’s the real deal. For now, at least, the machine’s running smooth, and no one’s dumb enough to test it."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks in the foundation, no panic in the halls. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the people at the top aren’t even sweating. But the sermons are getting sharper, and the books people ‘lent’ you lately? They’re not just for decoration. The regime’s not afraid of us—it’s afraid of *time*. And that’s the only thing we can’t control."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
